## Goal

Notebook 04 fixed the cells (1,555 stromal senders, 2,622 early lymphoid receivers, at most 500 per population) and the
L–R links (25 S5 pairs = 27 gene–gene links: the four claimed Notch pairs plus the highest S5 means). Here we follow the
CausalCCC tutorial steps, as in case study 1:

1. build a Seurat object from the exported counts;
2. select, in each group, the genes sharing the most mutual information (MI) with the genes of interest: the ligands
   (senders), the receptors and four Notch target genes (receivers) – `causalCCC.MIselection()`;
3. build the mosaic table and the state order (`causalCCC.mosaic()`, `causalCCC.state_order()`), with population,
   donor, chemistry and sequencing depth as metadata variables;
4. run MIIC with the settings of the CausalCCC web server (`scripts/run_miic.R`), on 8 threads.

In case study 1, some settings (number of selected genes, sender genes copied to the receivers, one thread) were chosen
to reproduce the authors' published network. They are not reused here: we keep only the SeuratObject fix and the
exclusion of ribosomal and mitochondrial genes, and otherwise use the package defaults.

The network is only summarised here; its interpretation is the subject of the next notebook.

**Inputs:** `results/thymus_early/04_runA_input/`.
**Outputs** in `results/thymus_early/05_runA_causalccc/`: MI tables, selected genes, the four files that the web server
takes (`causalccc_files/`), and the MIIC result (`miic_input/miic_result.rds`).

::: {.callout-note}
## Running time
Gene selection: about 10 to 20 minutes per group. MIIC: several minutes to half an hour on 8 threads. Both are saved the
first time and reloaded afterwards; delete `selected_genes.rds` or `miic_input/miic_result.rds` to recompute them.
:::

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(Matrix)
library(Seurat)
library(miic)        # load miic before causalCCC
library(causalCCC)

find_repo_root <- function(dir = getwd()) {
  while (!(file.exists(file.path(dir, "README.md")) && dir.exists(file.path(dir, "notebooks")))) {
    parent <- dirname(dir)
    if (parent == dir) stop("Repository root not found. Open the repository folder in Positron.")
    dir <- parent
  }
  dir
}

root <- find_repo_root()
# patch_causalccc(), written for case study 1, is reused unchanged: SeuratObject >= 5.3 fix for
# causalCCC.MIselection() and causalCCC.mosaic() (copies of the two functions, for this R session only)
source(file.path(root, "scripts", "case1", "case1_helpers.R"))
patch_causalccc()

input_dir   <- file.path(root, "results", "thymus_early", "04_runA_input")
results_dir <- file.path(root, "results", "thymus_early", "05_runA_causalccc")
dir.create(results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

senders   <- "stroma"
receivers <- "early_lymphoid"
metadata  <- c("population", "donor", "method", "n_counts")   # n_counts: total counts per cell (sequencing depth)
# Canonical Notch target genes in early T-cell development, added as genes of interest on the receiver side
notch_targets <- c("HES1", "DTX1", "NRARP", "PTCRA")
n_threads <- 8
set.seed(2026)
```

## 1. Seurat object

```{r}
#| label: seurat

counts <- readMM(gzfile(file.path(input_dir, "counts.mtx.gz")))
genes  <- read_csv(file.path(input_dir, "genes.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)$gene
cells  <- read_csv(file.path(input_dir, "cells.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |> column_to_rownames("cell")
dimnames(counts) <- list(genes, rownames(cells))

thymus <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = as(counts, "CsparseMatrix"), meta.data = cells)
rm(counts)
thymus
table(thymus$group, thymus$population)
```

```{r}
#| label: links

interact_edges <- read_tsv(file.path(input_dir, "interact_edges.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
ligands   <- unique(interact_edges$ligands)
receptors <- unique(interact_edges$receptors)
stopifnot(all(c(ligands, receptors) %in% rownames(thymus)))
interact_edges
```

## 2. Gene selection

For each group, `causalCCC.MIselection()` computes the MI between every gene and each gene of interest (the
"pivots"), and keeps the genes with the highest MI. The number kept is the package default,
`max(15, min(4 × number of pivots, 100))`.

Three choices:

- **Pivots: the ligands (senders); the receptors plus four Notch target genes (receivers).** HES1, DTX1, NRARP and
  PTCRA are classic Notch targets in early T-cell development (HES1 is also among the authors' DN markers). If the
  claimed DLL4/JAG2 → NOTCH1 signalling is active, NOTCH1 should connect to them in the lymphoid network. They are also
  kept in the network whatever the selection gives.
- **The metadata are not pivots.** They enter the network as variables (section 3), but they do not choose the genes.
  (`causalCCC.wrapper()` does use them as pivots. With donor as a pivot, the selection would add the genes that best
  separate donors, mostly sex-chromosome genes such as XIST, which tell us nothing about signalling.)
- **Ribosomal and mitochondrial genes are excluded from the selection.** In case study 1, ribosomal protein genes had
  high MI with almost any gene because of their high counts everywhere; mitochondrial genes mainly reflect cell quality.

```{r}
#| label: selection-input

is_ribo <- grepl("^RP[SL]", rownames(thymus)) & !grepl("^RPS6K", rownames(thymus))   # RPS6K*: kinases, not ribosomal
is_mito <- grepl("^MT-", rownames(thymus))
c(ribosomal = sum(is_ribo), mitochondrial = sum(is_mito))
stopifnot(all(notch_targets %in% rownames(thymus)),
          !any(c(ligands, receptors, notch_targets) %in% rownames(thymus)[is_ribo | is_mito]))
goi <- list(senders = ligands, receivers = unique(c(receptors, notch_targets)))
lengths(goi)   # at most 30 pivots per group
selection_input <- thymus[!(is_ribo | is_mito), ]
```

```{r}
#| label: selection
#| message: false

selected_file <- file.path(results_dir, "selected_genes.rds")
if (file.exists(selected_file)) {
  selected <- readRDS(selected_file)
} else {
  # n_genes is left at its default
  select_for <- function(group, pivots, colour) {
    causalCCC.MIselection(data_input = selection_input, assay_name = "RNA", interact_ident = "group",
                          oneinteract = group, goi = pivots, metadata_list = NULL,
                          save = TRUE, plot = TRUE, output_dir = file.path(results_dir, "MI_tables"),
                          color_heatmap = colour)
  }
  selected <- list(senders   = select_for(senders, goi$senders, "darkgreen"),
                   receivers = select_for(receivers, goi$receivers, "darkorange"))
  saveRDS(selected, selected_file)
}
rm(selection_input)

genes_senders   <- unique(c(goi$senders, selected$senders))
genes_receivers <- unique(c(goi$receivers, selected$receivers))
c(sender_genes = length(genes_senders), receiver_genes = length(genes_receivers),
  in_both = length(intersect(genes_senders, genes_receivers)))
```

```{r}
#| label: selected-genes

# Genes added by the selection (in addition to the pivots)
list(senders   = setdiff(genes_senders, goi$senders),
     receivers = setdiff(genes_receivers, goi$receivers))
```

## 3. Mosaic table and state order

The mosaic table has one row per cell. Sender genes are filled in the stromal cells and empty (NA) in the lymphoid
cells, and the other way round; genes selected in both groups get a `_senders` / `_receivers` suffix. The metadata
variables are added on both sides, so they also get the suffix (`donor_senders`, `donor_receivers`, …).

Population, donor and chemistry are unordered categories, so no level order is given.

**Sequencing depth (`n_counts`).** A first run without it showed a module of housekeeping genes (EEF1A1, TPT1, PTMA,
ATP5 subunits, H2AFY, …) whose counts follow the total count of the cell within each population: links joining two
such genes were twice as frequent as expected by chance, and three of the non-ligand neighbours of NOTCH1 (H2AFY,
MTF2, TFDP2) belonged to it. With raw counts, depth acts as a common cause of all genes; as a variable, MIIC can
explain those links by depth instead of linking the genes to each other. It is not a pivot, so the gene selection is
unchanged.

`causalCCC.state_order()` declares every metadata variable as discrete (`var_type = 0`); `n_counts` is a count, so it
is set to continuous (`var_type = 1`) afterwards.

```{r}
#| label: mosaic
#| message: false

mosaic <- causalCCC.mosaic(data_input = thymus, assay_name = "RNA", interact_ident = "group",
                           senders_name = senders, receivers_name = receivers,
                           genes_senders = genes_senders, genes_receivers = genes_receivers,
                           metadata_senders = metadata, metadata_receivers = metadata)

no_order <- setNames(rep(list(NULL), length(metadata)), metadata)
state_order <- causalCCC.state_order(mosaic_data_table = mosaic,
                                     metadata_senders = no_order, metadata_receivers = no_order,
                                     genes_senders = genes_senders, genes_receivers = genes_receivers,
                                     ligands = ligands, receptors = receptors)
state_order$var_type[str_starts(state_order$var_names, "n_counts")] <- 1
filter(state_order, group == "metadata")

# L-R links with the same (suffixed) names as the mosaic table
edges_out <- interact_edges |>
  mutate(ligands   = if_else(ligands %in% genes_receivers, paste0(ligands, "_senders"), ligands),
         receptors = if_else(receptors %in% genes_senders, paste0(receptors, "_receivers"), receptors))
stopifnot(all(c(edges_out$ligands, edges_out$receptors) %in% names(mosaic)))

dim(mosaic)
count(state_order, group, var_type)
```

The four files taken by the CausalCCC web server are saved as well, so the same run can be repeated there.

```{r}
#| label: save-files

files_dir <- file.path(results_dir, "causalccc_files")
dir.create(files_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.table(mosaic, file.path(files_dir, "causalCCC_df.csv"), quote = FALSE, sep = ",", row.names = FALSE)
write.table(state_order, file.path(files_dir, "causalCCC_st.tsv"), quote = FALSE, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE)
write.table(edges_out, file.path(files_dir, "causalCCC_interactEdges.tsv"), quote = FALSE, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(causalCCC.layout(state_order, network_height = 8), file.path(files_dir, "causalCCC_layout.json"))
list.files(files_dir)
```

## 4. MIIC

MIIC runs with the settings of the CausalCCC web server (`scripts/run_miic.R`) on 8 threads. With more than one thread,
MIIC crashed in case study 2 ("C stack" errors): R's limit on the C stack (8 MB by default) is too small for the worker
threads. Lifting that limit for the MIIC process only (`ulimit -s unlimited`) removes the crash. On the case study 1
input, a run on 8 threads with the lifted limit gave the same network as the single-thread run of case study 1
(notebook 04 of case study 1): the same 497 retained links, with the same orientations and information values, in 6.6
instead of 26 minutes. The only difference was in the `confidence` column (33 of 6,181 rows, by at most 0.02), which
comes from random shuffles that are distributed differently between threads; it changed none of the retained links.

Case study 2 (notebook 10) fixes the same crash differently: a patched `miic` (`envs/patches/miic/`, `docs/INSTALL.md`,
section 4) that makes multithreaded runs give the one-thread links, orientations and genuine causations, with only the
`confidence` column differing. The two approaches agree; this notebook uses the installed `miic` with the lifted stack
limit.

```{r}
#| label: miic

miic_dir    <- file.path(results_dir, "miic_input")
result_file <- file.path(miic_dir, "miic_result.rds")
dir.create(miic_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!file.exists(result_file)) {
  files <- file.path(miic_dir, c("input.tsv", "state_order.tsv", "interact_edges.tsv"))
  write_tsv(mosaic, files[1], na = "NA")
  write_tsv(state_order, files[2], na = "NA")
  write_tsv(edges_out, files[3], col_names = FALSE)
  command <- paste("ulimit -s unlimited &&", "Rscript", shQuote(file.path(root, "scripts", "run_miic.R")),
                   paste(shQuote(files), collapse = " "), shQuote(miic_dir), n_threads)
  if (system2("bash", c("-c", shQuote(command))) != 0) stop("MIIC failed, see the messages above.")
}
miic_result <- readRDS(result_file)
attr(miic_result, "run_time")
```

```{r}
#| label: summary

edges <- miic_result$all.edges.summary |> filter(type == "P")
lr_keys <- paste(edges_out$ligands, edges_out$receptors)
tibble(retained_links   = nrow(edges),
       lr_links         = sum(paste(edges$x, edges$y) %in% lr_keys | paste(edges$y, edges$x) %in% lr_keys),
       variables_linked = n_distinct(c(edges$x, edges$y)),
       variables_total  = ncol(mosaic))
```

The L–R links are imposed by CausalCCC (they connect variables that are never observed in the same cell); what MIIC
learns is the network around them, within each group. Which genes and metadata connect to the ligands and receptors –
and in particular to the claimed Notch pairs – is examined in notebook 06.
